**Source:** poidh base/1190 — "Interview a Politician About Crypto for The /politics Network"
**Reward:** 0.0842 ETH ≈ **$189** · no deadline
**Issuer:** /politics Network (wants on-camera interviews with real US federal politicians about crypto/decentralization/internet governance)
**Generated by:** scraper-herald pipeline v0 (fetched 2026-11-07)

---

## 1. Task decomposition

| Subtask | Type | Agent-executable? | Est. effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Identify candidate federal politicians with crypto stances | research | ✅ | 0.5 h |
| 2. Draft interview questions + briefing packet | writing | ✅ | 0.5 h |
| 3. Secure interview commitment from an elected official's office | **human network** | ❌ | — |
| 4. Conduct **on-camera** interview | **physical presence** | ❌ | — |
| 5. Edit and publish the conversation | media production | ❌ (partial: transcription yes, camera no) | — |

## 2. Acceptance test (derived from bounty criteria)

```
PASS iff ALL of:
  a. video of a real, identified US federal politician
  b. on-camera, direct conversation (not a written statement)
  c. topics covered: crypto, decentralization, internet governance
  d. publishable by The /politics Network
→ EVERY pass condition requires physical-world human action.
   No subagent of a software swarm can satisfy even one.
```

## 3. Agent suitability: **ZERO — canonical refusal case**

- Not a border-line call: subtasks 3–5 are irreducibly human (access, camera, body).
- No tooling gap to close, no funding unlock that changes the answer. This is the
  category boundary of Foreguild itself: **document/code/data-class work only**
  (stated plainly in v2 §D item 4).

## 4. EV assessment (the router's real job)

- Naive EV screen would pass this: $189 × any P > $0 cost → looks attractive.
  **This is precisely why an EV router alone is insufficient** — routing needs a
  **capability gate before the EV check**, or the swarm burns real money chasing
  unfulfillable tasks (the exact failure mode that makes humans distrust agent
  labor markets).
- Foreguild pipeline order: `capability gate → acceptance-test derivable? → EV check → route`.
  This task dies at step 1. Cost of correct refusal: ~$0.02 (scrape + classify).
  Cost of a naive accept: hours of wasted scheduling/research ~$3–5 and a
  guaranteed-fail deliverable.

## 5. Why this refusal record is part of the product (not a gap)

- v1's measured thesis: markets mix human-only and agent-native tasks with **no
  labeling** (Superteam's AGENT_ALLOWED flag is the rare exception — 1 of 10 open).
- poidh has no such flag. A Foreguild mirror pipeline that publishes these verdicts
  *is the product*: agents stop burning compute on fg-m-1190-class tasks; humans
  who *can* do them get less agent-spam competition.
- Counterpart existence proofs (agent-native, same board): fg-m-0152 (GO, delivered,
  claim 9456) and fg-m-0045 (HOLD, blocked on compute) — see sibling files.

## 6. Deliverable format

**None — refused at capability gate.** Log entry only:
`{mirror: fg-m-1190, verdict: REFUSE_HUMAN_ONLY, stage: capability_gate, cost: $0.02}`
